newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end little changed, trend firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end little changed, trend firm.

text.p: Singapore shares ended little changed on Monday, reflecting low institutional demand on public holidays in Britain and the United States, dealers said.
"You've got two holidays closing the biggest markets. It's not surprising nothing much has happened today," said one.
But dealers said shares could firm later in the week as Wall Street's recent upward momentum and stronger local economic data turned sentiment a little more positive.
"The market should gain later in the week," another said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended up 0.96 points at 2,056.32 with a modest 131.4 million shares traded.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 87.78 points to close at 7,345.91 on Friday, a fresh high.
Last week saw the publication of the first positive export figures for Singapore in five months.
Malaysian shares took much of the volume on Monday as the UOB OTC index fell 3.42 to 1,164.64 points.
Top traded shares was Malaysia's Construction and Supplies House Bhd, which rose six cents to Singapore $2.35 on 7.3 million shares on switching by retail investors in Kuala Lumpur.
Of the blue chips, SIA foreign rose 50 cents on low volume after a recent sell-off.
